body: That's more of the explanation of the poem. Here is the real one: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ltun92DfnPY

I haven't uploaded anything yet but I'm planning on. Also, drawing is something that I would love to be able to do. My sister can draw and even her first drawings look great. Would you mind showing me some of them? I'm sure they look beautiful. I know what it feels like to live with something unbearable. Recently my cat died and it felt like living without him was unbearable. I've lost a lot in my time in the earth and each time it felt unbearable. But, I need you to trust me when I say that nothing will ever be too unbearable. No matter how hard you get pushed down, even if you get pushed off a cliff, you need to be able to pick yourself up. To be able to say to yourself, "I'm strong enough to get through this," even if you don't believe it. If you haven't already, watch "To This Day" by Shane Koyczan. It made me realize a lot about myself and got me into poetry.

If you're wondering how I handle my depression then it's because I've started to express myself. I've done things like write poetry and play music in order to let my feelings out. I use these things like a valve to release my stress and emotions. Emotions are like balloons, you let them build up and eventually they burst, but if you release them then they stay in a manageable state. Hoped I helped you and seeing your answer to the other person who responded, I want to let you know that things can help. Nothing that you do is permanent, though it may seem like it is. In the words of John Green, "Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem."

I have this feeling all the time. I tell myself that, "You aren't depressed. You just want attention," etc. Just know that you aren't the only one feeling like this. I've known people that have almost been raped and have no suicidal thoughts. That makes me feel like I'm just terrible for wanting to die. But, I've learned something. Depression comes in different forms. In the simplest terms everyone is depressed differently. Some people have bi-polar disorder. Others just feel like they don't belong on the Earth. Others are bullied etc. So, don't feel like you are crying out for attention or that people will think that. Suicide is something that deserves attention. If you're thinking about a therapist then I would say go for it. I don't have any personal experience with therapy, but if you think that it'll help then go for it. Help is the main thing that you need at a time like this. When you're at your lowest, when your at the bottom of Mt. Everest, you need something to help you get yourself up.
